checks: Borrowed bounded request parser completes body/tag validation before semantic mutation; unsupported controller versions close before mutation.
Checked wire epoch +1 and nonempty-log epoch +1 mappings preserve empty (0,0); initialization synchronizes internal term1 before readiness.
Fixed distinct signed32-bit membership and successor bounds are enforced before controller mutation; count32/33 are explicitly excluded from native shift wrapping.
Votes reuse synchronized election journal transitions and poisoned ambiguous-failure handling; same-term repeated/different candidate behavior is covered by independent fixture responses.
Known same-epoch leader conflicts return local42; differing prior vote does not bar following an asserted trusted elected leader and the durable prior vote remains.
Caller-driven incoming RPC adapter has no autonomous polling/outbound peer loop or replication/commit authority; actor queue is bounded and storage is on a blocking thread.
Actor cancellation skips unstarted replies; in-progress storage cancellation is ambiguous. Shutdown stops admission, wakes the actor, retains its join handle across cancellation and joins on retry.
Peer replies validate full schema, correlation, partition, fixed identities, leader/grant consistency and epoch before distinct-voter counting; stale grants cannot elect a newer candidate.
Epoch overflow checks fence unrepresentable outgoing state; higher-term demotion precedes timer/persist ambiguity in trusted-adoption and existing election paths.
limits: Queue caps concern admitted payload lengths/counts, not a process RSS ceiling or all caller allocation capacities.
Filesystem synchronization can block; request cancellation does not abort an active fsync.
Operator must bind journal path to the same cluster/topic/epoch representation; node IDs are not authentication.
Only exact fixture/native handler results and documented static-profile transitions are qualified; no complete KRaft interoperability.
